question: After the document structure is repaired, should OpenClaw accept the revised one-package/one-new-agent Claws contract and require the experimental prototype stack to migrate to it?
rationale: Document correctness cannot determine whether the proposed CLI, manifest, ownership, provenance, lifecycle, and migration semantics should become permanent OpenClaw policy.

options.title: Accept and restack
options.body: Approve the central complete-agent contract, define prototype migration and scoped deferrals, create the implementation issue, and advance the RFC through acceptance.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC draft while maintainers resolve additional portability, schema-ownership, and migration details.

options.title: Decline first-class Claws
options.body: Do not establish a unified Claw lifecycle and instead contain or remove the experimental prototypes.

recommendation.title: Accept and restack
recommendation.body: Approve the central complete-agent contract, define prototype migration and scoped deferrals, create the implementation issue, and advance the RFC through acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the governing RFC process and have the strongest repository-wide history for routing the final acceptance decision.
